# Establishment log — popol-vuh-017 (image 0053 from line 16, 0054, 0055, and 0056 to about line 26)

Read 2026-11-27 by the routine's own model from source/pages/i0053 (l.16 to the foot), all of i0054 and i0055,
and i0056 to `… xqui tic vi canoc.`, in strips of about seven lines at 1.0×, with 1.5–3× crops of doubtful words,
checked word by word against Brasseur 1861 (OCR lines c. 24562–24575, 24640–24680, 24760–24790, 24900–24930,
24990–25010). Pillow in a scratch venv (the system PIL is broken in this container).

Start: `Que quicot chicut xe bec echaahel` (0053 l.16, Ximénez's indented paragraph). End: `… xa pa chaquih vleu chu
nicahal vpa cochoch xqui tic vi canoc.` (0056, mid-line), the end of Brasseur's chapter 7 (the twins plant the two
canes); the next words, `ta xe be cut huhun chi vvb chique, xe cah chi Xibalba`, begin the descent to Xibalba
(Brasseur's chapter 8), where popol-vuh-018 should begin. parts.json: 018 set to images 0056–0059 (was 0060–0062,
which would have left 0057–0059 unread); plan.md row updated. Image 0057 not needed.

Content: the twins play ball on their fathers' court; the lords of Xibalba hear them and send messengers to summon
them in seven days; the messengers come by the road the boys made and tell Xmucane; the grandmother, grieving, sends
a louse; the louse is swallowed by a toad (Tamazul), the toad by the snake Zaquicaz, the snake by the falcon (vac);
the falcon lights on the ball court, cries `vacco`, is shot in the eye, healed with rubber (loꜩ quic), and disgorges
the snake, which disgorges the toad; the toad cannot bring up the louse, which is in its gums; the message is
given; the twins go home to take leave and plant two canes in the middle of the house, signs of their life or death.

Paragraphs: Ximénez indents `Que quicot chicut` (0053 l.16), `Catepuch xqui vvbah ri vac` (0055 l.4) and
`Hona ix catit` (0056 l.11); the other breaks are ours, at the sense joints (as 015 and 016 did).

## Folios
Counting as 004–016 did (0053 = 22r): 0054 = 22v, 0055 = 23r, 0056 = 23v → `fols. 22r–23v`. The crop of 0056
carries `23` at the top left (the folio doubt in QUESTIONS.md, 2026-11-24, again); the earlier count is kept.

## Letter-forms of this hand (applied throughout)
- Ximénez's **t** often looks like an h with a faint cross: `que petic` (0053, MS looks `pehic`), `xi petic` ×2 and
  `xe petic` (0056), `xchi ca tic` ×2 (0056, MS looks `cahic`), `que tio` (0054, looks `quehou`), `chu tiho` (0055,
  looks `chuhho`). Read as t where Brasseur has t.
- His **r** often looks like v: `xꜭha ri atit/catit/vac` (MS looks `xghavi` ×4), `naqui pa ri choquic` (looks `vi`).
- **a/u** are ambiguous: `xu tic` (0056; MS looks `xa`), `xul tacol` (0055; looks `xal`), `curi` (0054 l.44; looks
  `cari`) — Brasseur's u taken each time. `xe chaahic` (0053 l.17) looks like `chauhic`; Brasseur's chaahic taken.

## Letters decided against Brasseur (image followed)
- **g-shaped = ꜭ** (B. q / ch'): `ꜭaholab`, `ꜭahol`, `vꜭux`, `ruꜭ`, `cuꜭ`, `ivuꜭ`, `vꜭ` 'louse' (B. Uq) throughout;
  `ꜭo ba` ×4 and `ꜭo vi`, `ꜭo retal` (B. qo); `xeꜭha`/`xꜭha`/`caꜭha`/`quixꜭha`/`xuꜭhax` (MS gh); `ꜭhanic` (0055;
  B. ch'anic); `ꜭaxtoy` (0055; B. qaxtok); `xꜭhacachob` (0054; B. x-chakachob — letter for letter, **doubtful**);
  `Caꜭhau oc` (0055; B. Ca chau-oc).
- **`ꜫuz choc`** (0054 l.3): the letter is g-shaped, which this hand uses for ꜭ, but Brasseur's g and 015's `ꜫuz`
  decided ꜫ.
- **plain ch where the formula is usually gh**: `quecha ahauab`, `quecha ri ahauab` (0053), `cacha vzamahel`
  (0054), `cacha ri ivatit` (0055), `xuchax` (0055). Printed as written.
- **plain c/qu where B. has g/q/k**: `ca tocol` (B. togol), `qui quih` (B. gih; as 016's `quih`), `xoc` / `v oquibal`
  / `choquic` (B. x-og, r'ogibal, ch'ogic — the word is oꜫ 'cry'), `coquic`, `mix oquic`, `caztah` (B. qaztah),
  `cazlic`, `cochoch`, `catit`, `bico`/`xbic`/`xa bic` (B. bigo/big), `chaquihic`.
- **ꜩ (tz ligature)**: `Vꜩ bala` ×3, `nu ꜩih` ×5, `vꜩih`, `ca ꜩih` ×2, `ꜩiquin`, `v ꜩuꜩil hom`, `chi ꜩelet`,
  `xqui ꜩonoh`, `loꜩ quic`, `vꜩ chic`, `Caꜩihon oc`, `ca ꜩihon oc`, `chu caxꜩ`. Plain z: `xqui mez`, `nimarizah`,
  `zamahel`, `Zaquicaz`, `zcaquin`, `xqui zucah` (B. tzukuh), `ca ziquinic`, `huzu`, `caztah`, `cazlic`, `ꜫuz`.

## Doubtful readings
- `mi xu tiquiba` (0053 l.19): MS `mixuhquiba` — the h-like t with no i; Brasseur `tiqiba`. Printed tiquiba
  (README 5b: a dropped letter); the drafter's note should open with the MS reading.
- `He cu itaca chic` (0053 l.23): an ink blot covers the letter after `he`; Brasseur `He cu y taka`.
- `que chahic` (0053; B. qu'echahic 'they were eating'): division unclear (que echahic?).
- `nima hoc` (0053; B. nima 'hoc): sense unclear.
- `chi malmat ib` (0054 l.6): MS `chimalmatib`; Brasseur's division taken.
- `que tio v cumatz` (0054), `que bico v xpec` (0054): Brasseur's division (u = their/its).
- `xꜭhacachob` (0054 l.43): perched? (B. x-chakachob, s'abattit).
- `Naqui pa ri choquic` (0055 l.2): MS `chogquic` or `choquic`; read choquic.
- `Caꜭhau oc` (0055): MS `caghauoc`.
- `chu caxꜩ vchi` (0055 l.24): MS `chucaꜩ` with an x written above the a (supralinear, printed in place);
  Brasseur `chu qaxah u chi`. Word and sense uncertain.
- `xrah chaiic` (0055; B. chayic 'beat'): letters as written.
- `ta xiic vvarachac chi acan` (0055 l.28): MS `xiic` clear; Brasseur `x-yicu va r'achak`; `vvarachac` (×2) meaning
  unclear (Brasseur: 'his back/spine', échine).
- `chava re xpec` (0055; B. chuva re): MS `chavare`.
- `xa v chac cumatz xuxic` (0055 l.38): Brasseur `xa u bi cumatz`; the image has `v chac` clearly.
- `chi caztah vvach` (0056 l.2): MS `catzatz v/vach` or `caztahz`; read caztah after Brasseur qaztah.
- `ix pu ca chuch` (0056): `pu` is in the MS, not in Brasseur.
- `xticou Xbalanque` (0056 l.17): MS `xti/cou` across the line break; Brasseur `x-ucou`. Letters as written.

## README 5b correction
- `Hunahpu` (0056 l.17): MS `hun nahpu` (n doubled across the word space), corrected; the unit's note should open
  with the MS reading.

## Brasseur's omissions and differences (image followed)
- `ix pu ca chuch` (B. omits pu); `xa v chac cumatz` (B. xa u bi cumatz); `ta xiic` (B. ta x-yicu va).
- Nested direct speech (the lords' words inside the messengers', the louse's message) is printed inside one pair
  of “ ” — the pin check admits no single quotes; the drafter marks the levels in `i`.
